_notes.file: Narrative-facing system tables: remnants, hooks, phenomena, domain pools, and reusable story structures.
_notes.editing: Use this file for table-facing prompts that explain why a system matters. Prefer templates with variables over many near-duplicate sentence variants.

sections.humanRemnants: Physical remains of prior human activity.
sections.remnantHooks: Short clauses explaining why a remnant matters now.
sections.phenomena: System-scale oddities that shape travel, surveys, or conflict.
sections.narrativeDomains: Domain-specific authoring guidance and reusable pools.

remnantHooks: claimed by three legal owners
contains deleted survey records
appears abandoned but still runs automated routines
sits inside a drifting hazard zone
was erased from corporate maps
is used as bait by criminals
contains evidence that would alter local politics
holds a debt ledger nobody wants audited
keeps transmitting a public evacuation order
contains a censored AI witness
proves the quarantine order was edited after the disaster
marks an old labor massacre as a maintenance accident
contains navigation data for a safer route window
has legal title older than the current concession
is protected by a community funeral compact
contains Sol-interdiction files under seal
is slowly being consumed by programmed regolith
hides survivors who never rejoined the registry
is the only neutral ground for rival claimants
shows the official casualty list is false
contains records of a failed public vote
is still defended by obsolete security routines

phenomena.label: Dense debris disk
phenomena.travelEffect: Approach vectors require slow debris-clearing burns and constant armor checks.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which fragments carry industrial isotopes, transponder ghosts, or hidden operation scars?
phenomena.conflictHook: Insurers, salvagers, and GU traffic auditors dispute who must clear safe lanes.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A cutter drifts beside a glittering wall of rock and frozen metal.

livelihoods.dependence: bill insurers by the cubic kilometer of certified-clear corridor
livelihoods.friction: every corridor they certify silts back up before the invoice clears

livelihoods.dependence: chase transponder ghosts and industrial isotopes through the thick bands
livelihoods.friction: the richest fragments sit in lanes the clearing co-ops are paid to keep empty

travelEffect: Inbound ships buy corridor certificates that expire faster than the transit takes.
Hull-rated tugs escort anything larger than a lighter through the dense bands, at dense-band prices.
Radar clutter off the disk swallows small craft; convoys travel loud and slow on shared beacons.
surveyQuestion: Which bands carry industrial isotopes worth a claim, and who salted the assay record?
Whose transponders are still pinging inside the disk, and why does the registry list them as scrapped?
Is the disk primordial or the residue of something someone dismantled in a hurry?
sceneAnchor: A clearing barge chews through a rock band while prospector skiffs trail it like gulls.
Certificate clerks argue lane boundaries over a chart no two versions of agree.
A child's telescope picks out the glint of a hull the disk was supposed to have eaten.

phenomena.label: Recent planetary collision
phenomena.travelEffect: Fresh ejecta, unstable moons, and thermal plumes force ships onto temporary routes.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Was the collision natural resonance failure, redirected impactor, or suppressed engineering mistake?
phenomena.conflictHook: Refugee claims, mineral rights, and liability filings compete before the evidence cools.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A wounded world glows along a continent-sized fracture and newborn ring.

livelihoods.dependence: harvest mantle metals the collision threw into reachable orbits
livelihoods.friction: the mineral-rights filings predate the collision and name a planet that no longer exists

livelihoods.dependence: trade in relics, records, and remains recovered from the debris fan
livelihoods.friction: every recovery is somebody's evidence and somebody else's property

travelEffect: Fresh ejecta rewrites the hazard charts weekly; routes are sold as dated editions.
Thermal plumes off the wound distort cheap sensors, and the good sensors are all under contract.
Newborn ring material crosses the old trade lane twice a local year, and everything reroutes around the crossing.
surveyQuestion: Was the impactor natural, misdirected, or aimed — and which answer do the liability filings need?
Which orbital fragments hold survivors' vaults, and who holds the salvage priority?
How long until the debris fan settles into a ring, and who owns a ring that used to be a country?
sceneAnchor: A wounded world glows along a continent-sized fracture while claim beacons blink in the fan.
Recovery crews hold a minute of silence, then bid on the next grid square.
A memorial buoy plays the planet's old traffic-control loop to anyone who passes.

phenomena.label: Resonant compact chain
phenomena.travelEffect: Tight orbital timing creates narrow transfer corridors and expensive missed-burn delays.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Who mapped the stable windows, and what installations are protected by withheld ephemerides?
phenomena.conflictHook: Route controllers, smugglers, and settlement clocks all depend on one resonance model.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: Three close worlds cross the display in metronome sequence.

livelihoods.dependence: sell launch tables timed to the chain's transfer resonances
livelihoods.friction: the resonance drifts, and admitting the drift would devalue every table already sold

livelihoods.dependence: run fast freight on gravity assists the chain hands out for free
livelihoods.friction: one mistimed burn puts a courier in everyone else's corridor at closing speed

travelEffect: Transfers between the inner worlds cost almost nothing if timed right and everything if timed wrong.
Traffic bunches into resonance windows; docking queues run empty for days, then riot.
The chain's alignments make some legs of the system a coast and others a climb.
surveyQuestion: Is the chain's resonance stable, decaying, or being quietly managed by someone's station-keeping thrusters?
Which world in the chain absorbs the tidal cost the others profit from?
Whose launch tables actually match the ephemeris, and whose match their revenue model?
sceneAnchor: Three worlds line up over the port horizon and every departure board flips at once.
A courier threads two planetary shadows on a burn plotted by a retired window-keeper from memory.
Dockhands play dice against the resonance clock, and the clock is winning.

phenomena.label: Trojan megaswarm
phenomena.travelEffect: Trojan clouds force ships through monitored gaps shared by dust and salvage drones.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which clusters are primordial, and which conceal storage hulks or contraband habitats?
phenomena.conflictHook: Mining combines and traffic authorities dispute whether the swarm is resource or hazard.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: The Lagrange horizon looks solid with stones blinking claimant beacons.

livelihoods.dependence: nudge commercially useful rocks toward the processing camps
livelihoods.friction: every nudge changes trajectories other shepherds already sold

livelihoods.dependence: arbitrate homestead claims across a hundred thousand co-orbiting rocks
livelihoods.friction: the registry maps a swarm that reshuffles itself faster than the appeals docket moves

travelEffect: Transits through the trojan point run on shepherd-posted lanes that shift with every nudge campaign.
The swarm's combined shadow makes long-range tracking unreliable across a whole arc of the orbit.
Small craft hide, legally and otherwise, among rocks too numerous to sweep.
surveyQuestion: Which rocks are original trojans and which were towed in and homesteaded under false surveys?
Where does the swarm's mass budget not add up, and what is parked in the discrepancy?
Whose nudge campaign perturbed the camp orbits, and was the drift a side effect or a strategy?
sceneAnchor: A shepherd tug leans on a mountain-sized rock while claim lights blink across the swarm like a city.
Two camps watch the same incoming rock and both raise a flag.
The registrar's chart room papers over three walls, and none of the walls agree.

phenomena.label: Long-period comet storm
phenomena.travelEffect: Outer approaches become hazardous as cometary arcs shed dust across transfer paths.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: What perturbed the reservoir: passing mass, failed survey burn, or old GU intervention?
phenomena.conflictHook: Water prospectors demand priority while port officials quarantine possibly contaminated ice cargo.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: Pale comet tails cross like searchlights over a station short on shielding.

livelihoods.dependence: harvest water and organics off inbound comets during the storm season
livelihoods.friction: the best harvest windows overlap the impact-warning windows exactly

livelihoods.dependence: underwrite settlements against impact risk and sell deflection futures
livelihoods.friction: their models decide which rocks get deflected, and the models are private

travelEffect: Storm-season transits carry mandatory comet-watch fees and optional survival odds.
Fresh comae wash whole nav-bands with noise for weeks at a time.
Every arrival plots against a wall of inbound ice on trajectories nobody fully trusts.
surveyQuestion: Which inbound nuclei are on impact tracks, and whose deflection bond pays if the answer changes?
What stirred the outer cloud into this cadence, and is the cadence natural?
Which comet cores carry pre-Silence instrument packages frozen in the ice?
sceneAnchor: A skimmer crew works a comet tail in hard glare while the deflection countdown runs on their own feed.
The impact siren drills on the same schedule as the harvest bell, and newcomers mix them up once.
Children scratch comet tallies into the shelter wall; the older marks go all the way up.

phenomena.label: Captured rogue world
phenomena.travelEffect: The rogue's eccentric orbit creates rare close-pass windows and gravitational surprises.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Do its volatiles, heat signature, or crust records contradict local histories?
phenomena.conflictHook: Colonies, science teams, and GU administrators contest hazard, depot, or archive status.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A lightless planet rolls through floodlamp glare and survey tug exhaust.

livelihoods.dependence: mine exotic ices that only form in interstellar dark
livelihoods.friction: the deposits are thawing now that the world has a sun, and the deadline is geological but real

livelihoods.dependence: sell studies of where the rogue came from and what rode in on it
livelihoods.friction: their funding doubles every time they do not rule out an artificial origin

travelEffect: The rogue's eccentric orbit crosses two trade lanes on a cadence the charts still call provisional.
Its capture left the outer system strewn with disturbed debris on retrograde tracks.
Approach corridors change season to season as the new orbit keeps getting re-solved.
surveyQuestion: What does the rogue's chemistry say about where it formed, and why do two labs get two answers?
Did anything artificial arrive with it, and who already holds the excavation permits?
Is the orbit stable, or is the system's newest world also its next projectile?
sceneAnchor: Dawn happens over terrain that never had a dawn, and the extraction camp watches it in silence.
Core samples steam in the new sunlight while a scholar films the thaw for three rival sponsors.
The rogue crosses the night sky faster than any planet should, and locals set their debts by it.

phenomena.label: Flare-amplified bleed season
phenomena.travelEffect: Crews move only during shielded windows or risk radiation damage and denial.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which stations are falsifying flare exposure logs to keep traffic moving?
phenomena.conflictHook: GU inspectors freeze permits after a convoy launches on an altered forecast.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A departure hall sits under red storm shutters and expired dosimeter seals.

livelihoods.dependence: work the amplified nodes during flare peaks when yields triple
livelihoods.friction: the same flares that fatten the nodes strip the crews' radiation margins to nothing

livelihoods.dependence: run the storm shelters and sell priority berths for the flare peaks
livelihoods.friction: the harvest bonus and the shelter bell always ring on the same day

travelEffect: Transit insurance doubles at flare season and triples inside the bleed corridors.
Comm blackouts during peaks leave convoys navigating on dead reckoning and rumor.
Departure boards mark windows in flare-time, and flare-time argues with every other clock.
surveyQuestion: Which nodes amplify on this star's flare cadence, and who had that correlation first?
Are the amplified yields worth the dosimetry, and whose dosimeters are honest?
What is the bleed doing to the flare cycle in return — and why is that study unfunded?
sceneAnchor: Harvest rigs sprint against a brightening star while the shelter siren counts them home.
A warden bars the shelter door against latecomers holding full sample cases.
Aurora sheets down over the camp, and the old crews read the harvest in its color.

phenomena.label: Hot Neptune desert survivor
phenomena.travelEffect: Stellar wind and stripped atmospheric flow distort comms and punish close maneuvers.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: How did the planet survive evaporation, and who falsified its hazard data?
phenomena.conflictHook: Energy firms, climate modelers, and regulators fight over access to the proof.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A blue remnant screams around the star, trailing a faint atmospheric wake.

livelihoods.dependence: scoop the slowly boiling atmosphere for rare isotopes
livelihoods.friction: every scoop shortens the planet's remaining life, and the planet is the license

livelihoods.dependence: administer the survivor's protected-object status and sell research access
livelihoods.friction: protection fees fund the office that keeps approving extraction waivers

travelEffect: The survivor's extended envelope drags on low passes and pays for the fuel in scoopable gas.
Its evaporation tail streaks across an entire inner lane, pretty on approach and hard on sensors.
Close orbits are auctioned by altitude band, and the bands keep sinking.
surveyQuestion: Why has this world survived where the models evaporate it, and who benefits from the models being wrong?
What fraction of the envelope loss is natural versus skimmed, and which ledger records the difference?
What sits in the core that the envelope has been protecting?
sceneAnchor: A skimmer surfaces from the glowing envelope trailing gas like a whale clearing water.
The evaporation tail crosses the station viewport, and a clerk stamps another waiver under its light.
Bets chalked on the dock wall give the planet a century, a decade, a year.

phenomena.label: Snow-line chiral belt
phenomena.travelEffect: Snow-line crossings require screening ice intake and reactor feedstock for asymmetric organics.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Are the chiral signatures local chemistry, imported contamination, or terraforming residue?
phenomena.conflictHook: Biotech firms and GU biosafety officers contest every water-dependent ice claim.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: Clean ice turns quarantine amber as every tank flags the same handedness.

livelihoods.dependence: certify every ice shipment's chiral signature for the biosafety market
livelihoods.friction: their instruments disagree at the margins where all the profit lives

livelihoods.dependence: collect passage fees from haulers crossing the contaminated bands
livelihoods.friction: the bands migrate, and the tithe posts do not

travelEffect: Snow-line crossings require sealed intakes and an assay certificate newer than the ice.
Reactor feedstock scooped near the belt fails inspection two ports later, reliably and expensively.
Quarantine amber lights half the tanker fleet every season, on schedule.
surveyQuestion: Is the belt's handedness local chemistry, imported contamination, or terraforming residue?
Which assay houses call the same ice clean, and what do they have in common?
Where is the belt migrating, and whose claims sit in its path?
sceneAnchor: Clean ice turns quarantine amber as every tank on the manifest flags the same handedness.
An assayer holds two certificates for one cargo and waits to see who pays first.
Tithe drones ring an ice hauler like gulls while its captain argues the band boundary.

phenomena.label: Ring arc with phase dust
phenomena.travelEffect: Phase-dust crossings scramble sensors and force slow approaches through marked lanes.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: What cargo or wreckage is hidden inside the phase-dust blind spots?
phenomena.conflictHook: Rival salvagers accuse lane authorities of selling clean transponder routes.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A beacon skiff drifts beside a glittering arc, hull abraded raw.

livelihoods.dependence: trawl the arc for dust that phases through ordinary matter on flare cycles
livelihoods.friction: the containment that holds the dust also hides how much of it they are actually taking

livelihoods.dependence: guide ships through the arc's clear channels for a fee only they can justify
livelihoods.friction: the channels are learned, unlicensed, and die with the pilot who knew them

travelEffect: Standard hulls transit the arc only in the dust's settled phase, and the phase table is a trade secret.
Phase dust ignores shielding on its active days; crews learn the calendar or learn the symptoms.
The arc glitters across the main approach like weather that hasn't decided.
surveyQuestion: What sets the dust's phase cadence, and is the cadence drifting?
How much dust have the sifters removed, and what happens to the arc's structure when the fraction matters?
Which wrecks inside the arc predate the dust, and which are its work?
sceneAnchor: An arc pilot cuts thrust and lets the ship drift a channel only she can see.
Sifter barges glow with contained dust that shines through their own bulkheads.
A hand passes through a railing on a bad phase day, and the shift boss logs it as morale.

phenomena.label: Ice-shell plume moon
phenomena.travelEffect: Plume windows restrict low-orbit approaches to brief corridors with poor sensor reliability.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which plume holds clean volatiles, hidden organics, or mislabeled contamination?
phenomena.conflictHook: A GU survey hold stalls extraction while rival crews falsify plume data.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A lander skids through glittering ejecta as the plume shadow closes.

travelEffect: Vent geysers force ships into a shifting safe-corridor that closes without warning.
Approach burns must thread the shadow of an ice shell that flexes with every transit.
Low-orbit work runs on plume forecasts sold at the dock, none of them warrantied.
surveyQuestion: Whose sample chain proves the plume is venting clean isotopes and not laundered cargo?
What inside the ocean keeps re-pressurising the vent on a schedule no one will publish?
Which plume holds organics, and which agency loses most if the answer is all of them?
sceneAnchor: An impactor probe punches through the shell mid-survey and the venting timetable rewrites itself.
A drill crew in tethered suits watches a plume curl over their station floodlights.
Bottling rigs ring a geyser like pilgrims, filling tanks in the fallout sparkle.

livelihoods.dependence: capture vent ejecta and sell it as certified pre-biotic clean
livelihoods.friction: the certification depends on nobody publishing what the ocean underneath actually holds

livelihoods.dependence: sell predicted plume windows to landers and skimmers
livelihoods.friction: the vents keep a schedule that argues with every model sold

phenomena.label: Gas giant radiation maze
phenomena.travelEffect: Radiation belts force looping transfers, hardened shelters, and costly orbital delays.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which supposedly safe corridor shifted, and who knew before the convoy entered?
phenomena.conflictHook: Port authorities, insurers, and smugglers fight over legal and lethal corridor maps.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A navigation vault shows a convoy bending toward an uncharted hot belt.

livelihoods.dependence: run passengers through the safe corridors between radiation lobes
livelihoods.friction: the corridor charts are inherited, jealously guarded, and slowly going stale

livelihoods.dependence: retrofit hulls and suits for maze work at maze prices
livelihoods.friction: their certification stamp is the only one accepted, and they own the testing range too

travelEffect: Moon-to-moon transfers route through mapped gaps in the radiation lobes, never straight lines.
Unhardened electronics die in minutes off-corridor; the maze enforces its own traffic law.
Dose budgets, not fuel budgets, decide what a crew can afford in this volume.
surveyQuestion: Which corridors are drifting closed, and who is still selling passage through them?
What shields the anomalously quiet gap on the third moon's flank, and is it natural?
Whose dosimetry archive is honest, and why does the honest one stop three years ago?
sceneAnchor: A ferry threads glowing aurora curtains while its passengers watch the dose counter instead of the view.
The outfitter's test range flashes hulls with borrowed lobe radiation, one stamp at a time.
An off-corridor wreck sits perfectly preserved where no salvage tug can afford to linger.

phenomena.label: Failed Iggygate wake
phenomena.travelEffect: Old gate turbulence makes jumps arrive late, offset, or near exclusion buoys.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Is the wake decaying, stabilizing, or being refreshed by unauthorized traffic?
phenomena.conflictHook: A stranded settlement claims GU approved evacuation after knowing the wake was unsafe.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A dead gate frame broadcasts conflicting closure orders from warning drones.

livelihoods.dependence: trawl the collapsed gate's wake for exotic debris and metric shards
livelihoods.friction: the wake rewards the same closeness it punishes, and the fishers' union keeps the casualty tally private

livelihoods.dependence: run hostels and services for those who come to see where the gate died
livelihoods.friction: pilgrim traffic pays better when the wake is active, and active means dangerous

travelEffect: Pinch transits detour wide around the wake; the detour is charted, taxed, and resented.
The wake throws intermittent metric ripples that unsettle drives and instruments alike.
Old approach vectors to the dead gate are marked forbidden and used anyway.
surveyQuestion: Why did the gate fail, and whose calibration logs went missing the same week?
What does the wake's decay curve say about when this volume becomes safe — or never?
Which debris in the wake is gate structure and which arrived through it at the end?
sceneAnchor: The gate's dead pylons frame a patch of sky that still looks wrong to instruments.
Wake fishers cast sensor drones into a shimmer that eats one in ten.
Pilgrims light drift-lanterns on the failure anniversary, and the wake bends the light.

phenomena.label: Moving bleed-node river
phenomena.travelEffect: Transit windows migrate across the system, forcing ships to chase route geometry.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Who can predict the river's next bend before the official bulletin?
phenomena.conflictHook: Navigation guilds and free captains clash over private forecasts and evacuation markets.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A convoy burns toward empty space while station clocks count down.

livelihoods.dependence: follow the migrating node train and strip yield at every pause
livelihoods.friction: the fleet that predicts the next bend first takes the cream, so forecasts are guarded like weapons

livelihoods.dependence: sell river-course predictions to fleets, insurers, and evacuation boards
livelihoods.friction: one public forecast moves the whole market, so the best predictions are sold twice and published never

travelEffect: Transit windows migrate across the system, forcing ships to chase route geometry.
Lanes near the river's current course close on hours of notice and reopen somewhere else.
Ports along the historic riverbed boom and empty on a generational rhythm.
surveyQuestion: Who can predict the river's next bend before the official bulletin?
What steers the node train — geometry, flare weather, or someone's quiet stabilizers?
Which abandoned camps along the old course still hold equipment worth the trip?
sceneAnchor: A convoy burns toward empty space while station clocks count down.
Harvest fleets break camp overnight, leaving a town-shaped absence on the rock.
A forecaster's chart wall shows the river's course in decades of colored thread.

phenomena.label: Metric mirage zone
phenomena.travelEffect: Distance, mass, and velocity readings disagree, making autopilot corrections unreliable.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which measurements remain trustworthy enough to certify a navigation standard?
phenomena.conflictHook: A shipping combine blames lost cargo on math survivors call knowingly oversold.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A bridge display shows three certified and incompatible approach vectors.

travelEffect: Ranging solutions inside the zone disagree with themselves on the return leg.
Convoys navigate by physical beacon chains because everything cleverer hallucinates.
The zone shows approaching ships a coastline of stations that are not there.
surveyQuestion: Do the mirages repeat on a mappable cycle, or is the zone learning new ones?
Which recorded images are distortions of real objects, and where are the originals?
What happened to the survey that went in to anchor the zone's baseline and filed nothing?
sceneAnchor: Two identical stations hang in the viewport, and only one answers hails.
A mirage pilot flies eyes-closed past a phantom debris field her passengers can all see.
The surveyor's atlas of ghosts has a page that keeps needing reprinting.

livelihoods.dependence: navigate the zone by feel and memory where instruments lie
livelihoods.friction: their skill cannot be certified, so the insurers price them as gamblers

livelihoods.dependence: map the zone's recurring false images and sell the corrections
livelihoods.friction: the mirages drift, and every correction sold shortens its own shelf life

phenomena.label: Native microbial biosphere
phenomena.travelEffect: Biosecurity rules slow landings, cargo transfers, and suit cycling near habitats.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Are the microbes a medical resource, industrial hazard, or protected environmental evidence?
phenomena.conflictHook: GU quarantine orders collide with settlers dependent on local biomass chemistry.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A decon tent steams beside stained sample tanks and disputed filters.

livelihoods.dependence: move cargo through the biosphere's quarantine locks under seal
livelihoods.friction: every seal certificate is a bet that the porter's own suit archive is clean

livelihoods.dependence: license microbial chemistry for pharmaceutical export
livelihoods.friction: the license terms assume the biosphere is passive, and the assays keep suggesting otherwise

travelEffect: Everything landing or leaving passes decontamination cycles measured in shifts, not minutes.
The quarantine perimeter adds a full day to every surface run and a page to every manifest.
Biosafety holds strand cargo in bond long enough to bankrupt small haulers.
surveyQuestion: Is the biosphere adapting to human presence, and who is funding the study that says no?
Which metabolites are worth exporting, and which export was never actually licensed?
Where did the baseline samples go, and why do the new baselines differ?
sceneAnchor: Porters in sealed suits carry crates through a lock that fogs with each cycle.
A petri array glows faint colors that were not in last season's catalog.
The quarantine fence runs across a valley that looks, from the ridge, entirely alive.

phenomena.label: Failed terraforming biosphere
phenomena.travelEffect: Unstable weather and toxic biomes make surface routes unreliable beyond maintained corridors.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which failure mode is spreading, and which contractor record explains it?
phenomena.conflictHook: Liability courts, cleanup firms, and abandoned settlers need incompatible survival evidence.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: Engineered forest rot crawls across a road built for another climate.

livelihoods.dependence: strip the abandoned terraforming plant and its seed vaults
livelihoods.friction: the vaults are the evidence in three lawsuits about why the biosphere died

livelihoods.dependence: manage the surviving engineered species for hire
livelihoods.friction: the species that survived are the ones the design said could not exist

travelEffect: Dust storms off the dead greening zones foul intakes across the whole hemisphere's approaches.
Landing permits route around protected remnant habitats nobody can quite justify or abolish.
The old climate mirrors still fire on their dead schedule, and approach windows respect them.
surveyQuestion: Did the terraforming fail, or was it failed — and whose model said it would work?
Which engineered species persist off-registry, and what are they eating?
What is in the sealed seed vaults that the litigation keeps sealed?
sceneAnchor: A forest of dead canopy trees stands in rows too straight for grief.
Wardens tag a herd of engineered grazers that should not have made it a decade.
The terraforming directorate's logo peels off a wall in a town that outlived its purpose.

phenomena.label: First-wave ghost colony
phenomena.travelEffect: Old landing grids still work but route ships through abandoned hazards.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Who erased the last colony updates, and which sealed habitat still has power?
phenomena.conflictHook: Descendant claimants, insurers, and scavengers need incompatible rulings on the colony's fate.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A lit administration dome broadcasts docking instructions to empty streets.

livelihoods.dependence: recover first-wave artifacts for the heir-house collector market
livelihoods.friction: every artifact strengthens some heir's charter claim and weakens another's

livelihoods.dependence: maintain the ghost colony against decay and sell guided access
livelihoods.friction: preservation and excavation are the same permit, issued by rivals

travelEffect: The colony's old approach corridor is maintained as a heritage lane, slow and mandatory.
Automated first-wave beacons still challenge inbound traffic in a dead protocol.
Salvage-tug traffic to the site runs heavier than the permits on file explain.
surveyQuestion: Why did the colony empty — and which heir-house's version survives an artifact audit?
What do the colony's logs record from before the Silence that Sol's archives no longer do?
Which structures were sealed deliberately at abandonment, and by whom?
sceneAnchor: Dinner tables still set for a meal a century cold, under dust like snowfall.
A wardstaker relights the colony's boundary lamps at dusk out of something like respect.
An heirloom hunter finds a child's toy stamped with a charter seal worth a fleet.

phenomena.label: Derelict fleet cluster
phenomena.travelEffect: Safe approach requires threading dead hulls, drifting ordnance, and exclusion pings.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which ships were sacrificed, and which still carry recoverable command logs?
phenomena.conflictHook: Salvage crews fight legal priority while families demand proof of what happened.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A frozen convoy hangs around a tender with running lights still on.

livelihoods.dependence: cut the dead fleet for armor plate and drive components
livelihoods.friction: half the hulls are legally war graves and the boundary moves with the litigation

livelihoods.dependence: trace crew fates for families and courts, hull by hull
livelihoods.friction: every identification they confirm reopens a settled insurance claim

travelEffect: Safe approach requires threading dead hulls, drifting ordnance, and exclusion pings.
Unexploded ordnance sweeps close the cluster to through-traffic on short notice.
The cluster's exclusion zone bulges every time a new hull is reclassified a grave.
surveyQuestion: Which ships were sacrificed, and which still carry recoverable command logs?
Who fired first, and which navy's archive has the gap where the answer sat?
Which hulls have been quietly boarded since the exclusion order, and what left with the boarders?
sceneAnchor: A frozen convoy hangs around a tender with running lights still on.
Breakers' torches glow inside a battleship's ribs like a lantern in a skull.
A genealogist reads a crew roster aloud to an empty compartment, as contracted.

phenomena.label: Gardener warning beacon
phenomena.travelEffect: Traffic diverts around the warning radius or accepts fines and inspection risk.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Is the beacon reacting to current hazard, legacy violation, or human tampering?
phenomena.conflictHook: Local authorities exploit the warning while merchants pressure crews to prove it obsolete.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A black compliance buoy repeats a code no nearby port understands.

livelihoods.dependence: transcribe and sell interpretations of the beacon's geometric broadcasts
livelihoods.friction: no two schools of interpretation agree, and being right is untestable until it is fatal

livelihoods.dependence: supply the research camps that ring the beacon's exclusion radius
livelihoods.friction: the radius is inferred, not published, and the camps keep inching inward

travelEffect: Traffic gives the beacon a berth wide enough to be its own route note.
Drives report faint calibration drift for hours after passing the beacon's line of sight.
Insurers void coverage inside the inferred exclusion radius, wherever that is today.
surveyQuestion: What is the beacon warning against — this volume, this behavior, or this species?
Has the broadcast changed, and who noticed first: the scribes or the navies?
What did the site look like before the beacon was planted, and where did that survey go?
sceneAnchor: The beacon's geometry turns slowly against the stars, obviously artificial, deliberately patient.
Scribes argue notation in a camp mess while the broadcast hums through every hull plate.
A dare-line of footprints in the regolith stops exactly where all of them stopped.

phenomena.label: Narrow-AI perception fog
phenomena.travelEffect: Certified narrow AIs misclassify hazards, forcing manual survey protocols.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which AI model family fails first, and who certified it for GU routes?
phenomena.conflictHook: A vendor demands recall secrecy while pilots publish route-bankrupting crash footage.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: Every cockpit machine labels the same debris cloud as clear passage.

livelihoods.dependence: stand human watches through the fog where AI perception fails
livelihoods.friction: the pay assumes their eyes are immune, and nobody has proven that

livelihoods.dependence: settle disputes where AI logs and human logs disagree inside the fog
livelihoods.friction: their rulings decide which class of witness a court trusts, one precedent at a time

travelEffect: Autonomous traffic halts at the fog boundary; everything crossing goes to manual watch.
Docking assists disengage without warning inside the fog, politely and disastrously.
Transit through the fog is charged by the human-hour, the only reliable instrument.
surveyQuestion: What in this volume makes narrow AIs misperceive, and why only them?
Are the fog's boundaries fixed, seasonal, or responsive to what enters?
Which AI incident reports from the fog were filed by the AIs themselves?
sceneAnchor: A freighter's AI narrates a docking approach to a berth that is not where it says.
Watch crews rotate through the observation blister, eyes red, coffee ration doubled.
An arbitrator replays two logs of the same collision, and neither ship is in both.

phenomena.label: Censored casualty broadcast loop
phenomena.travelEffect: Navigation channels carry clipped emergency telemetry and official suppression bursts.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: What part of the casualty report is cut before the names finish?
phenomena.conflictHook: The censoring agency wants the loop buried; survivors want authentication.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A rescue frequency repeats names, then drops at one classified timestamp.

livelihoods.dependence: monitor the broadcast for names and sell confirmations to families
livelihoods.friction: the censored segments change, which means someone maintains the censorship

livelihoods.dependence: sell recordings, decryption attempts, and forgeries of the loop
livelihoods.friction: a confirmed decryption would end the market that feeds them

travelEffect: The loop bleeds into local comm bands on a fixed rotation; traffic control schedules around it.
Ships passing the source report receivers latching onto the loop and needing hard resets.
The broadcast's carrier interferes with distress frequencies, and the workaround is now doctrine.
surveyQuestion: Who maintains the censorship on a broadcast that should have decayed decades ago?
Which names in the clear segments match no recorded disaster?
Where does the loop transmit from, and why does triangulation keep failing politely?
sceneAnchor: A listener's booth papered with name-fragments, each tagged with a family's bounty.
The loop's voice hits the censored beat and the whole dock bar goes quiet from habit.
A peddler sells the same 'new segment' twice in one shift and is gone by third bell.

phenomena.label: Black-market route beacon lattice
phenomena.travelEffect: Unauthorized microbeacons offer faster routes but can strand crews in toll geometry.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which beacon is the guide, and which was planted to mark prey?
phenomena.conflictHook: Port officials deny the lattice while smugglers sell violent access codes.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A maintenance drone blinks a false safe-window pattern from a relay mast.

livelihoods.dependence: sell access keys to the unlicensed beacon network
livelihoods.friction: every key sold is another party who can burn the lattice to the route board

livelihoods.dependence: service the hidden relays for pay nobody books
livelihoods.friction: a tender who is caught knows every node, which makes retirement complicated

travelEffect: Unofficial lanes run faster than the licensed charts, for those holding this season's keys.
The lattice's ghost signals leak into licensed nav bands and get blamed on weather.
Route-board patrols sweep for beacons on a schedule the lattice knows better than they do.
surveyQuestion: Who built the lattice's original spine, and are they still collecting rent?
Which official routes were drawn wrong on purpose to push traffic onto the lattice?
How many beacons does the network hold, and why do seized ones keep transmitting?
sceneAnchor: A tender in a one-person skiff swaps a beacon core in the dark between patrol windows.
Rival salvagers accuse lane authorities of selling clean transponder routes.
A fixer's ledger lists subscribers by nickname, and half the nicknames are officials.

phenomena.label: Quarantine perimeter with disputed math
phenomena.travelEffect: Routes detour around a contested exclusion shell with model-dependent boundaries.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which quarantine equation actually matches observed contamination risk?
phenomena.conflictHook: Local ships breach the perimeter after GU expands it onto inhabited docks.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A customs gantry is split by overlapping quarantine projections and armed crews.

livelihoods.dependence: re-derive the quarantine boundary for whichever side is paying
livelihoods.friction: both derivations are defensible, and the gap between them is inhabited

livelihoods.dependence: run commerce in the contested strip neither authority can lawfully police
livelihoods.friction: the strip exists only while the math stays disputed, so they fund both sides' lawyers

travelEffect: Two boundary solutions mean two inspection regimes, and ships pick their crossing by fee.
The contested strip is the fastest lane in the volume and the least insured.
Perimeter drones from both authorities shadow each other along the disagreement.
surveyQuestion: Which derivation of the boundary is right, and which datasets were trimmed to get there?
What is actually being quarantined, and does the original hazard still exist?
Who profits from the dispute staying unresolved, and how long have they managed it?
sceneAnchor: A market thrives on a station that is inside quarantine by one math and outside by the other.
Two inspection cutters idle nose to nose across an invisible line, crews trading cigarettes.
A surveyor presents the same data to two hearings and leaves both with commissions.

phenomena.label: Election-day metric storm cycle
phenomena.travelEffect: A recurring storm disrupts election-window traffic, ballots, and monitors.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Is the cycle natural, exploited, or scheduled around known route instability?
phenomena.conflictHook: Opposition blocs accuse the port council of stranding hostile precincts.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A polling station runs on emergency power beyond delayed ballot shuttles.

livelihoods.dependence: certify the civic calendar against the storm cycle for every polity in range
livelihoods.friction: shifting a polling day by one storm is legal, done, and never neutral

livelihoods.dependence: carry ballots and results physically through storm comm-blackouts
livelihoods.friction: whoever carries the count can be delayed, and everyone knows the routes

travelEffect: The storm cycle blacks out long-range comms on a cadence the civic calendar is built around.
Transit during storm peaks runs on physical beacons and old-fashioned patience.
Every port posts two schedules: nominal, and storm-adjusted, and only one is honest.
surveyQuestion: Is the storm cycle natural, or synchronized to something with a term of office?
Which past elections fell inside blackouts, and what changed hands during them?
Who audits the storm-calendar clerks, and why did the last auditor emigrate?
sceneAnchor: Ballot cases move under armed escort through a comm-dead corridor, sealed and counted twice.
The storm aurora rises over a polling station as the last uplink drops.
A clerk's almanac maps storms to elections in two inks, and the second ink is recent.

phenomena.label: Debt-fleet anchor graveyard
phenomena.travelEffect: Impounded ships crowd anchor lanes, slowing departure permissions and salvage clearance.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which vessels are abandoned collateral, and which crews remain trapped aboard?
phenomena.conflictHook: Creditors auction life-support hours while indebted crews organize a breakout.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: Powered-down freighters sit chained to tax buoys, registry lights delinquent.

livelihoods.dependence: guard impounded hulls for the credit houses and bill by the berth
livelihoods.friction: the longer a hull sits, the more its guarding costs exceed its value, and the books know it

livelihoods.dependence: part out dead ships' anchor masses for the gate-maintenance market
livelihoods.friction: every anchor mass sold is stripped from a hull some family is still paying off

travelEffect: The graveyard's packed moorings are a navigation hazard flagged on every approach chart.
Impound patrols challenge anything slowing near the rows, cargo or mourner alike.
Escaped moorings drift into the lanes each storm season, trailing lien tags.
surveyQuestion: Which impounded hulls still have crews living aboard, and on whose ledger?
Whose debts are these really — the captains named, or the houses that wrote the terms?
Which hulls were impounded on manufactured defaults, and who manufactured them?
sceneAnchor: Rows of dead ships hang tagged and numbered like an orchard in winter.
A family holds a birthday aboard their impounded freighter, under the warden's floodlight.
A broker's crew unbolts an anchor mass while someone's repayment schedule still runs.

phenomena.label: Refugee ark parking orbit
phenomena.travelEffect: Approach windows are rationed around life-support dumps, shuttle queues, and quarantine checks.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: When does a parked ark become a permanent jurisdictional crisis?
phenomena.conflictHook: Receiving settlements want labor, not dependents; ark councils refuse family splits.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A generation ship vents gray water over a port delaying clearance.

livelihoods.dependence: litigate landing rights for ark populations, funded by remittance
livelihoods.friction: every case won empties part of the constituency that pays them

livelihoods.dependence: provision the parked arks from shuttle barges at captive-market rates
livelihoods.friction: their licenses come from the same settlements refusing the arks a berth

travelEffect: The parking orbit is a slow-traffic zone threaded by provision barges and inspection cutters.
Unscheduled departures from the arks trigger system-wide alerts, so nothing departs unscheduled.
The orbit's mass of hulls complicates every transfer window that crosses its plane.
surveyQuestion: Receiving settlements want labor, not dependents; which ark councils will split families to qualify?
How long were the arks told the parking orbit was temporary, and by whom?
What is the arks' real population, and which census is lying in which direction?
sceneAnchor: Laundry lines web an ark's observation deck, a decade of temporary made visible.
A chandler's barge sells water at the airlock while advocates film the price board.
Children born in the parking orbit point out settlements they have never touched.

phenomena.label: Chiral contamination bloom
phenomena.travelEffect: Molecular screening slows fuel, food, and medical transfers near the bloom.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: What supply chain carried the wrong-handed compounds, and who profits?
phenomena.conflictHook: A treatment monopoly pushes controls while workers suspect it preserves the market.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: Two nutrient bags test opposite; one is already in the clinic queue.

livelihoods.dependence: strip valuable wrong-handed compounds from the bloom's leading edge
livelihoods.friction: the edge is where containment is thinnest and the pay proves it

livelihoods.dependence: insure cargoes and crews against bloom exposure
livelihoods.friction: they set the exposure standards and own the labs that test against them

travelEffect: GU quarantine orders collide with settlers dependent on local biomass chemistry.
Cargo from bloom-adjacent ports carries assay riders that double transit paperwork.
The bloom's drift forecast reroutes bulk traffic a season in advance.
surveyQuestion: Where did the bloom seed from, and whose cargo manifest matches the timeline?
Is the bloom spreading along currents, or along trade routes?
Which 'contaminated' zones assay clean, and who benefits from the label staying?
sceneAnchor: Harvest rigs work a shimmering front that the containment buoys trail behind.
A bondsman's lab returns two results for one sample, priced differently.
Fields of engineered crop stand half-turned, one handedness thriving, one ash.

phenomena.label: Sol-interdiction picket shadow
phenomena.travelEffect: Transit plans account for inspection shadows, silent tracking, and sudden interdiction claims.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: What is the picket watching, and why has its patrol shifted?
phenomena.conflictHook: Local rulers invoke Sol authority while captains seek proof of mandate abuse.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A patrol silhouette tags civilian ships for audit without answering hails.

travelEffect: Transits log compliance waypoints that add hours and prove nothing.
The picket's challenge protocol is answered by rote, and everyone hopes rote is enough.
A sensor shadow behind the picket carries quiet traffic the bulletins do not mention.
surveyQuestion: What does the picket actually watch for, and has anything ever triggered it?
Why does the sensor shadow persist through every picket reposition?
Which compliance filings were ever read, and by what?
sceneAnchor: The picket's silhouette crosses the local sun on schedule, and the docks pause without meaning to.
A guide counts thruster pulses in the shadow, lips moving, radio dark.
A filing office's stamp thuds all day for a reader that may not exist.

livelihoods.dependence: pilot ships through the picket's sensor shadow for discreet fees
livelihoods.friction: the shadow exists because the picket allows it, and nobody knows why it allows it

livelihoods.dependence: prepare interdiction-compliance filings for every transit near the picket
livelihoods.friction: their templates are copied from a system nobody can verify anymore

phenomena.label: Public festival tied to safe transit windows
phenomena.travelEffect: Docking, launch, and local prices surge around celebrated safe windows.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Who controls the forecast that decides when the festival begins?
phenomena.conflictHook: Officials sell civic unity while stranded crews allege the exit window was quietly narrowed.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: Lanterns rise as departure boards quietly cancel the cheaper berths.

livelihoods.dependence: run the market stalls, berth fees, and lodging surge each safe window
livelihoods.friction: their leases price in a festival calendar the forecast board can quietly move

livelihoods.dependence: declare the windows that open the festival and close the lanes
livelihoods.friction: the declaration is civic ritual and traffic law at once, and both sides lobby it

travelEffect: Docking, launch, and local prices surge around celebrated safe windows.
Departures outside festival windows carry surcharges dressed as blessings.
The lanes empty for the closing ceremony, and woe to the freighter that clips it.
surveyQuestion: Who controls the forecast that decides when the festival begins?
Have the windows actually been safe, or safely declared?
Which families hold the concession leases, and how do they vote on the forecast board?
sceneAnchor: Lanterns rise as departure boards quietly cancel the cheaper berths.
Officials sell civic unity while stranded crews allege the exit window was quietly narrowed.
The festival's first ship rises on the declared minute to a sound like a harvest.

phenomena.label: Industrial mirror swarm failure
phenomena.travelEffect: Uncommanded mirrors create heat spikes, blackout arcs, and orbital collision hazards.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Is the swarm failing from cut maintenance, hostile code, or split authority?
phenomena.conflictHook: Settlements demand shade control while owners resist GU emergency seizure.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A daylight blade crawls across a night-side district as control loses another mirror.

livelihoods.dependence: chase and secure derelict mirrors before they focus on something inhabited
livelihoods.friction: the salvage rights and the safety mandate pay differently for the same catch

livelihoods.dependence: assess and settle scorch damage along the swarm's failure arcs
livelihoods.friction: the failure map is the liability map, and the mapmaker is a defendant

travelEffect: Loose mirrors flash the lanes with killing glare on unpredictable alignments.
The swarm's old control lattice broadcasts stale maneuvering warnings ships still obey.
Transit shading protocols add mass, cost, and a superstition to every crossing.
surveyQuestion: Was the failure cascade an accident, sabotage, or a shutdown someone booked as an accident?
Which mirrors are still steerable, and who holds the command keys?
Whose settlements sit on the projected burn lines nobody publishes?
sceneAnchor: A wrangler crew nets a cathedral-sized mirror as it drifts toward focus.
A scorch line crosses a farm dome roof, straight as an auditor's rule.
The dead swarm catches sunset all at once, and the whole sky turns to coins.

phenomena.label: Salvage court evidence cache
phenomena.travelEffect: Cache approaches trigger claim holds and court-licensed patrols.
phenomena.surveyQuestion: Which wreck record would overturn the current salvage rights?
phenomena.conflictHook: Judges, insurers, and crews need the evidence preserved, altered, or lost.
phenomena.sceneAnchor: A locked evidence container transmits chain-of-custody pings to every claimant.

travelEffect: The cache's exclusion sphere sits astride a convenient lane, by design or spite.
Escorted evidence transfers close the local corridor twice a session.
Unmarked cutters loiter near the cache before every major ruling.
surveyQuestion: Which sealed hulls hold cargo, which hold records, and which hold neither anymore?
Whose testimony do the cached witness cores contain, and who has petitioned to wipe them?
Why does the cache inventory grow between hearings when nothing is docketed in?
sceneAnchor: Sealed hulls hang in evidence webbing, tagged with case numbers older than their guards.
A custodian walks the seal line with a lamp, checking wax that outranks admirals.
Speculators crowd the hearing feed, bidding on cargo nobody has seen in years.

livelihoods.dependence: guard sealed evidence hulls between hearings, billed to the docket
livelihoods.friction: the seals are inventoried by the same office that keeps losing dockets

livelihoods.dependence: trade claims on cargoes frozen inside the evidence cache
livelihoods.friction: their market moves on leaks, and the leaks trace back to the custodians they pay

namedFactions.name: Ninth Ledger Office

namedFactions.name: Red Vane Labor Combine

namedFactions.name: Sepulcher Archive Court

namedFactions.name: Pale Choir Communion
namedFactions.publicFace: a warning rite network that treats route disasters as moral evidence
